target_customer: Independent fashion designers who submit designs, and shoppers who pre-order them; the YC page also describes brands sourcing apparel manufacturers
problem: Fashion retail carries inventory risk and overhead. Fabricly crowdsourced designs and used voting or pre-orders so items were made only if enough people ordered.
business_model: marketplace with designer commission of 5 to 15 percent per sale plus margin on made-to-order goods

founders.name: Ari Helgason
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page and TechCrunch (2010-11-18); no background given.

founders.name: Tom Riley
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page as CTO. No other source found.

competitors.name: Garmz
competitors.what: European startup with a similar crowdsourced fashion model

technical_complexity.rationale: A web storefront with voting and pre-order charging if a threshold is met; the hard part was working with factories in Los Angeles and New York, per TechCrunch.

defensibility.rationale: The model copied Threadless style crowdsourcing and Garmz already existed; supply relationships with factories gave some friction but no network effect was shown.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Fabricly.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (2010-11-18) framed it as reversing fashion's excess inventory model; no demand figures were given.

branding.domain_note: Used fabricly.com as the exact .com; it now shows a shutdown notice.
branding.community_and_virality: TechCrunch compared it to Threadless; nothing further found.

brand_strength.rationale: Only launch funding coverage was found, and searches return other brands such as Fabric.com.

outcome_analysis: Fabricly raised a 400,000 dollar seed led by Atomico Ventures in November 2010 for a crowdsourced, pre-order fashion marketplace. Its website now says Fabricly has shut down, with no date or reason, and no post-mortem or press was found, so the cause is not public and no failure factor is assigned.
notes: The seed round is from TechCrunch with Atomico as lead; an aggregator (parsers.vc) lists Y Combinator and 400K total, consistent with it. The YC page describes the company as a marketplace for sourcing apparel manufacturers and materials, which differs from the TechCrunch crowdsourced fashion description; the order of any change is not documented, so no pivot is recorded. The garmz source is the TechCrunch Nov 2010 article, about 9 months after the batch.
